summary: Choose a result value using explicit conditions.
syntax: CASE WHEN condition THEN result ELSE fallback END
documentation: CASE selects a result from the first matching WHEN condition. An ELSE clause provides a fallback when none match; without ELSE the fallback is NULL.
inputs: Ordered conditions and their result expressions.
returns: One chosen result value for each input row.
caution: WHEN conditions are checked in order. Put a more specific condition before a broader one when they overlap.
scenarios: Translate internal status codes into useful report labels.
Show different text for paid and unpaid records.
title: Label payment follow-ups
problem: Return id and a column called action: "Complete" when status = 'paid', otherwise "Follow up". Include NULL statuses in the fallback and order by id.
goal: Use CASE or an equivalent approach that demonstrates the same concept.
hint: Use a WHEN branch for paid and an ELSE branch for every other status.
starter:
-- Write one SELECT query against the example tables.
SELECT 1;
